invariant: A bracket inside a sequence arrow is one ordered arrow-configuration expression, not a color literal. CommandArrow captures the complete bracket body independently of the arrow shaft and applies it after deriving the shaft's base body, heads, direction, and decorations. CommandArrow.applyStyle tokenizes the body on commas. At the pinned Java revision, `dashed` and `dotted` select ArrowBody.DOTTED, `hidden` selects ArrowBody.HIDDEN, `bold` is accepted without changing the configuration, and every other accepted token is resolved as a color; later tokens operate on the configuration produced by earlier tokens. Color and body are therefore orthogonal and survive together for ordinary, self, reversed, bidirectional, and external sequence messages. The bracket is part of the arrow header only, so Creole anchors such as `[[#anchor label]]` in message text are not arrow styles.
causal_divergence: The original Rust parser treated an inline bracket as a color-only annotation, so `-[#C2185B,dashed]>` became invalid color `#C2185B,dashed` plus a solid body; external parsing discarded the bracket. Commit 59169b2a introduced typed source-order tokens, but its correction scans the entire pre-colon header and removes the first style-looking bracket anywhere. Java's CommandArrow grammar captures ARROW_STYLE only between ARROW_BODYA and ARROW_BODYB, after PART1 and before PART2. The fresh quoted-participant counterexample therefore leaves `Source [hidden]: 9401` intact in Java but Rust strips `[hidden]` from the participant and loses the first message. The first corrective pass confined style extraction to the arrow slot, but Rust's heuristic diagram dispatcher still scores a style-looking bracket in a participant as component evidence on a plain-arrow line. CommandArrow accepts the whole line as a sequence command; the dispatch-equivalent Rust predicate must therefore recognize the complete ordinary-message grammar, not merely ask whether its arrow happens to contain a style. Its two shaft alternatives each contain an `ARROW_BODYA` or `ARROW_BODYB` matched by `-+`; a recognizer that accepts decoration characters without any hyphen misclassifies ordinary words such as `footer` through their `o` characters. Four additional orthogonality gaps surfaced. First, SeqParser::autoactivation_for handles only Solid and Dotted; Java CommandArrow tests the head and then treats every non-dotted body, including HIDDEN, as activation under `autoactivate on`. Second, the fresh right-to-left bidirectional message is parsed as BOTH but Rust paints only one head when the source lies geometrically right of the target; ComponentRoseArrow draws dressing1 and then dressing2 for BOTH_DIRECTION independent of spatial order, and each dressing contributes its own line inset. The first corrective pass restored both shapes but emitted them in reverse dressing order and retained the single-head right inset. Third, Rust's external constraints use only the unnumbered label width. Java Step1MessageExo always builds its arrow component from AbstractMessage.getLabelNumbered, so the bold autonumber prefix and gap reserve left extent for found messages and right extent for lost messages. For a right-border arrow, MessageExoArrow.getLeftStartInternal additionally starts from the live segment's pos2; LivingParticipantBox.getLiveThicknessAt moves that origin to the active bar's right edge. Rust currently measures from the lifeline center, accounting for the residual five-pixel deficit after adding the number. Fourth, Rust closes activation records left open at page end on the last message ordinate. DrawableSet.drawLifeLineU instead calls LifeLine.finish(getMaxY()), extending every unfinished segment to the common diagram-body maximum; this accounts for the remaining uniform 9px activation deficit without a fixture-specific offset. These causes explain the rejected review's dispatch failure, activation nesting and terminal heights, external horizontal extent, and bidirectional ordering/inset diffs. The bold self-message itself is byte-equivalent on reinspection; the preceding bidirectional group caused the shifted structural diff.
planned_change: Parse inline style only as part of the arrow slot. Extend the ordinary and external message grammars to capture an arrow token containing its optional bracket between shaft halves; split and apply style tokens from that captured token, never by scanning participant or label text. Make UML subtype detection call the same complete-message recognizer used by the parser: a line is sequence evidence and cannot contribute bracket-component evidence only when its captured arrow contains the mandatory hyphen shaft, regardless of whether the arrow itself has a style. Preserve color and body as separate fields; apply comma tokens in source order, map dashed/dotted to DOTTED, hidden to HIDDEN, bold to the pinned no-op, and let later colors win. Treat HIDDEN as a non-dotted normal-head message for autoactivation while suppressing only its painter. Paint dressing1 then dressing2 for BOTH direction regardless of whether the sender is left or right, and inset the shaft independently for both painted heads. During both first-participant found-message and last-participant lost-message constraint calculation, evolve the normal autonumber state and include the current numbered-label prefix width and gap, matching getLabelNumbered before Step1MessageExo measures the component; anchor a lost message's width at the sender's live-segment right edge at that event. Represent activation records that remain open at page end explicitly and close them at the renderer's common diagram-body boundary, matching LifeLine.finish(getMaxY()) rather than adding a literal offset to the last event. Do not special-case review labels, participant names, message counts, source coordinates, or rendered coordinates.
